criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a new test through the real checks path (not a unit stub) asserts the producer's build directory does not exist when the first check starts and the candidate's work tree still exists afterwards.
criteria.evidence: Both pass (1 test each). The new test drives Athena::go with a real `sh -c` check. The check exits 1 if any <root>/jobs/*/target/produce exists, or if its working directory (the verifier snapshot) lacks the candidate's 'A demo' README. The job Landed. The 'disk       removed the producer's build directory' line precedes the 'checks     ' line, which only happens when the counting producer's planted target/produce existed and was removed. produce_dir no longer exists, and the committed records hold the candidate. Without the change the check would see target/produce, exit 1, and the job would be rejected. The test does not directly assert that jobs/<id>/work still exists; 'kept' is shown by the candidate's files being present at check time and the candidate being in the records.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a new test with a deliberately failing check asserts the drain log line contains the failing test name (not just 'test FAILED') and the job's committed records contain the last 200 lines of that check's output (a longer output is truncated to its final 200 lines).
criteria.evidence: The new test passes. It asserts the 'checks     ' ui line contains 'probe FAILED: demo::the_failing_one'. That ui is the one drain.rs passes into athena.go (drain.rs:2993), so the line reaches the drain log. It loads Records at HEAD (the committed records) and asserts the failed check's output_tail has exactly 200 lines, from 'output line 107' to 'after 5', with the FAILED line at index 194 and lines 1 and 106 absent. All 29 core checks unit tests pass, covering tail_lines, the 200-line tail via a real run_check, the 64 KiB ceiling, log_entry naming and fallback, and the +N more cap.

criteria.criterion: git diff shows the CHANGELOG.md entry describing both changes, and changes limited to crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs, crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, tests, and CHANGELOG.md (plus any record type needed).

findings.summary: The producer's build directory is removed after the disk check that runs before the checks, so that check can hold a job for low disk while this job's own idle build is still counted.
findings.evidence: The disk check runs at line 1308, and its sweep keeps the asking job's own build directory (disk.rs:477-479). free_producer_build runs only at line 1358. A job with about 10 GB in target/produce and too little free space is held, then the next drain's reclaim frees it and resumes. That costs a retry round, not correctness. Calling free_producer_build before the disk check would avoid it.

summary: The change removes the producer's build directory (target/produce) before the first check, whether the checks pass or fail. A failed check's committed record keeps its last 200 lines, with a 64 KiB ceiling. The drain's `checks` line names failing tests, taken from the recorded failed tests or from the harness's `test X ... FAILED` lines, and falls back to the check name. I ran both new tests through Athena::go with real sh checks; both pass. The removal test's check fails if any target/produce exists, so it would fail without the change. The failing-check test asserts the `checks` line names `demo::the_failing_one` and the committed record holds exactly lines 107 to 306 of a 306-line output. All 29 core checks unit tests pass, as do the updated ordering test and all 130 existing drain tests, including the low-disk and interrupted-job reclaim ones. fmt, clippy and the full test suite are recorded as passing in CI; I did not rerun them. There are only minor findings: (1) the removal runs after the disk check before the checks, and that check never removes the job's own build directory, so a job can be held when freeing it would have been enough; (2) run/mod.rs is outside the deliverables list but is the call site the checks stage needs; (3) a stale comment in the drain tests. The plan's test filters (`run::tests::<name>`) match 0 tests because the tests are in a submodule; I reran them by name.
